title: The Allowance a Standing Denial Earns on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Approval
content:
Where a denied decision already stands on a member's coverage determination record under a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan, an allowance is taken off the approval run, and its size is read from the member's fill history. The plan treats 3 or more fills standing paid for the contract year as settled therapy.

| A denied decision stands on the coverage determination record | Fills standing paid for the contract year | The allowance taken off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes, at least 1 | 3 or more | 60 days |
| yes, at least 1 | fewer than 3 | 30 days |
| no denied decision stands | any | nothing |

The plan's longer review allowance is 60 days and its shorter review allowance is 30 days. Where no denied decision at all stands on the record, neither is reached and no allowance is taken off, however long the member's fill history may be.

## Boundary cases on a hypothetical record

- A record carrying 1 denied decision and 4 fills standing paid: the allowance taken off is 60 days.
- A record carrying 1 denied decision and exactly 3 fills standing paid: the settled-therapy count is met, so the allowance taken off is again 60 days.
- A record carrying 1 denied decision and 2 fills standing paid: the count is not met, so the allowance taken off is 30 days.
- A record carrying no denied decision and 9 fills standing paid: no allowance is taken off.
